title: Tasked quest file (the legacy one-file format)
description: The one-file format, still read: one file under config/tasked/quests/ holding a whole questline. New packs should use the folder format instead - one group.json, one chapter.json and one quest per file - whose schemas are the `_schema/` set beside this one. A questline may be split across any number of these; the loader treats them as one tree and dependencies resolve across files.

$schema.description: Ignored by Tasked. For your editor, so it can autocomplete the rest of this file.

version.description: Format version. Written into new files. Present from the first release so that a future change has something to migrate from.

text.description: Either a plain string, or a translation key with an English fallback.

fallback.description: Shown if the translation is missing. Without it a player sees the raw key.

itemRef.description: An item, a count, and optional data components. Not an ItemStack — resolved at the moment it is used.

item.description: Namespaced item id, e.g. minecraft:oak_log. An item this build does not have keeps its id and the quest still loads: the row draws a placeholder and says the item is missing, so a removed mod can come back.

components.description: 1.21 data components, keyed by component id in the datapack's own spelling. A text component's value is a string holding JSON, as the codec writes it -- { "minecraft:custom_name": "\"Tempered Pickaxe\"" } -- and the editor writes that form when you pick a renamed item. Matched strictly: a task naming a renamed sword wants that sword and not a plain one.

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores. This id appears in player progress files, so changing it needs an entry in `aliases`.

namespacedId.description: A namespaced id, e.g. minecraft:oak_log or my_pack:chapter_one. The namespace is required, as it is everywhere this format names something by id.

dependencyStyle.description: One line's style. Only the axes it names override anything; the axes it omits fall back to the chapter's default, and then to the built-ins (chamfered, chevron at the target, solid, thin).

form.description: The route's shape. Chamfered is the built-in default: the three-segment step with every 90-degree corner cut at 45 degrees, a circuit trace. Orthogonal is the same step left square, straight a direct line, and curved a smooth bow, which reads `bend`.

arrowHead.description: The glyph an arrowhead is drawn as. Chevron is the built-in; none is a blunt line end.

arrowPlace.description: Where the heads sit: one at the dependent end (the built-in), one at each end, one in the middle of the route, or a repeating run.

arrowDensity.description: How far apart a stream repeats: 64, 32 or 16 pixels. Ignored by the other placements.

arrows.description: Legacy, read but no longer written: the single axis the three arrow axes replaced. None is a blunt end, one a chevron at the target, both one at each end, and many a stream at its old 24-pixel spacing.

dash.description: The line's pattern. Double is two hairlines either side of the route and ignores `weight`; hazard is the run plus diagonal hatch marks.

weight.description: How many pixels wide: 1, 2, 3, or a 6-pixel conduit with dark borders around a lighter core.

bend.description: How far a curved line bows, as a fraction of the chord between its ends. Positive bows one way and negative the other.

fromAnchor.description: The angle this line leaves its source node at, in degrees, 0 east and growing clockwise. Per line only. Absent means the automatic rim point.

toAnchor.description: The angle this line meets its target node at, in degrees, 0 east and growing clockwise. Per line only. Absent means the automatic rim point.

fromHandle.description: A split line's source-side control point, as [along, across] fractions of the line's own chord. `fromHandle` and `toHandle` are written together - one alone is a split with half a shape.

toHandle.description: A split line's target-side control point, as [along, across] fractions of the line's own chord.

themePatch.description: Token-level overrides for a chapter's theme: individual palette colours, a corner radius and a canvas background, applied over the named theme (or over the player's own when the chapter names none). A client concept, like `theme` itself - the server carries it and the client composes it. The validator checks every token id and value with the toolkit's own reader.

name.description: A name for the resulting palette. Usually omitted - the Chapter tab writes none, and the name only matters for a file that also wants a display name.

colours.description: Token id to colour, e.g. { "raised": "#FF24242E" }. A colour is #RRGGBB, #AARRGGBB, or a bare 0xAARRGGBB number. An unknown token id is reported by the validator, and the client ignores it.

canvasBackground.description: A pattern over the canvas's colour - the same object a theme file carries. `spacing` is content units under `graph` and screen pixels under `screen`; an image is screen-fixed and ignores it. The ink is the `canvasPattern` colour token, whose alpha is a pattern's strength - an image uses only its alpha and draws in white.

space.description: What the pattern is anchored to: the content, or the screen. Ignored by `image`, which is always screen-fixed.

spacing.description: Distance between repeats. Clamped to this range by the reader.

size.description: The edge of a dot or speck and the thickness of a line or hatch step, in pixels. Clamped to this range by the reader.

density.description: Speckle only: one cell in this many carries a mark. Clamped to this range by the reader.

direction.description: Hatch only: which way the diagonal leans.

fit.description: Image only: repeat the texture at `tile` size, or draw it once scaled to cover and centred.

texture.description: Image only: the texture id, canonicalised to `ns:textures/path.png`. An unresolvable texture draws nothing.

tile.description: Image only, under `tile` fit: the width one repeat is drawn at, in pixels. Clamped to this range by the reader.

cornerRadius.description: Corner radius in pixels for the chapter's surfaces. Zero is square.

motion.description: Transition duration in milliseconds. Zero disables transitions.

rewardTable.description: A roll of rewards: the table an inline-table reward carries. A weight-zero entry is always granted, once per roll call; every positive weight shares the rest of the probability space, and `lootSize` is how many times the dice are thrown.

emptyWeight.description: The chance of nothing on a throw, against the positive weights. Only tasked:loot includes it: a tasked:random promises something.

lootSize.description: How many times the dice are thrown.

title.description: What the table is called in the editor and on a reward's badge. Absent or blank falls back to the id, opened out: `tier_1_ores` reads as "Tier 1 ores".

icon.description: The item a browser row or a reward badge draws for this table. Absent means the first entry that has an item, then that entry's reward type's icon.

uid.description: The editor's handle for a table written `inline` in a quest or in another table: it is what the editor addresses when a reward sits above or below it in a list. A table in its own file under `reward_tables/` is addressed by its file name, does not use this, and the loader ignores it there.

weight.description: How much of the table's weight this entry takes. Zero means always granted, which is how a table says "and everyone also gets this".

reward.description: The reward this entry grants. All of anyType except two things. `conditions` cannot mean anything here: an entry is handed out by the roll rather than claimed, so a gate on it would be validated and then ignored. And `tasked:choice` cannot be an entry at all: a roll hands its entries out rather than offering them, so a choice entry is skipped. Put conditions on the table reward itself, and a choice on a quest.

condition.description: A gate on a task or a reward: every entry of a `conditions` list must hold for a player before the task counts for them, or the reward is paid to them. An empty list is met by definition.

type.description: The condition type's id, e.g. tasked:stage. The id decides which of the fields below mean anything.

count.description: tasked:item and tasked:item_tag (condition) — how many of them.

components.description: tasked:item (condition) — 1.21 data components, as on a task's item.

match.description: tasked:item (condition) — how closely a carried stack must match.

tag.description: tasked:item_tag (condition) — an item tag; any item in it counts.

objective.description: tasked:score (condition) — the scoreboard objective's name. An objective that does not exist reads as zero, so a typo locks the gate.

min.description: tasked:score and tasked:party_size (condition) — the number to reach: a score, or the members of the party online now. At least 1, so an objective that does not exist (which reads as 0) locks the gate rather than opening it. tasked:party_size is capped at 1000; tasked:score has no ceiling.

advancement.description: tasked:advancement (condition) — the advancement to have earned.

criterion.description: tasked:advancement (condition) — require one criterion of it instead of the whole advancement.

oneOf.description: One string per paragraph. Also accepts a bare string, for a one-line description. Markdown is read in these strings: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, [links](https://example.com), `#` headings and `- ` bullets.

description.description: A list of paragraphs, as a chapter's and a quest's are. A bare string is also accepted.

aliases.description: Former ids. Add one when renaming, and nothing that referenced the old name breaks.

icon.description: The item the book draws on the group's row. Optional: an absent icon falls back to the first chapter under the group.

collapsedByDefault.description: Whether the group starts folded in the sidebar. A reference group nobody reads front to back sets this; a player's own fold state is remembered over it.

description.description: One string per paragraph. Separate from a single newline-containing string on purpose. Markdown is read in these strings.

progressionMode.description: In a linear chapter the order of the quests list *is* the progression: each unlocks when the one above it completes, and no dependsOn is needed. A quest in a linear chapter that also declares dependsOn must satisfy *both*: the quest above it and its own edges. That is a real combination rather than a mistake — a linear spine with one quest that also needs something from another chapter — so nothing warns about it.

defaultPrerequisiteMode.description: What every quest in this chapter uses unless it says otherwise.

defaultConsumeItems.description: Whether item tasks in this chapter take the items unless the task says otherwise. The inherited default, which is why it lives here: an author sets it once for a whole trade chapter.

autoClaim.description: Whether this chapter's quests hand their rewards over on completion. `enabled` pays with a notification, `no_toast` silently, and `invisible` the same silence - the two silent names grant alike, the difference being FTB Quests' vocabulary rather than a behaviour; `disabled` waits for a claim, and `default` defers to the pack setting in index.json. A quest overrides this, and a reward's own `auto` overrides that. Rewards that need a decision - a choice reward - are never auto-granted whatever this says.

dependencyStyle.description: How this chapter's dependency lines are drawn unless a line overrides an axis. This is what a line's "Use chapter default" resets to. Only the axes named here are chosen: an axis left out falls back to the built-ins (chamfered, one, solid, thin), and a line that names the same axis overrides just that one.

dependsOn.description: The chapters this one waits on, by id or alias. Until the rule below is met every quest in this chapter is locked - it cannot be started, finished or claimed - whatever its own dependsOn says. A name that resolves to nothing is reported at load, because the chapter could then never be opened. The folder format's chapter.json carries the same fields.

prerequisiteMode.description: The rule over this chapter's own dependsOn, and *not* defaultPrerequisiteMode: that one is the mode this chapter's quests inherit for their quest dependencies, and this one is how many of the chapters above must be satisfied. all_completed is the default because a gate that let something through early is the surprising direction to be wrong in.

minRequired.description: How many of dependsOn must be satisfied, replacing the mode's own count - "any two of these three chapters". May not exceed the size of dependsOn, which is reported. It replaces the count and not the bar: the mode still decides whether a dependency has to be completed or merely started.

completesWhen.description: The quests that finish this chapter, by id or alias, in any chapter. The chapter reports completed once every one of them is; a repeatable quest counts after its first completion. Empty means the chapter never reports completed, which is a real state - it is then only ever satisfiable as "started". A chapter another chapter waits on as completed must declare this, and the loader reports the pair that does not.

hideUntilDependenciesComplete.description: Whether this chapter is left out of the book for a reader until its own dependencies are met. Off, it is listed and drawn dimmed with what it is waiting for on hover. An author in edit mode always sees it, or the flag could not be authored. Presentation only: the gate itself is enforced whatever this says. Not the same field as defaultHideUntilDependenciesComplete below: this one withholds the chapter's row, those decide what its quests do.

defaultHideUntilDependenciesComplete.description: What the quests in this chapter do about their own prerequisites unless a quest says otherwise: with it on, a quest here is hidden until its own prerequisite rule is met. A quest may write false to opt out, and a quest with no prerequisites is visible either way.

defaultHideUntilDependenciesVisible.description: The same default for hideUntilDependenciesVisible: with it on, a quest here is hidden until at least one of its prerequisites is itself visible.

theme.description: A palette this chapter asks to be drawn in. A client concept: the catalogue of themes lives on the client, so this is a plain string here and is reported by the client that could not resolve it.

themePatch.description: Token-level overrides for `theme`: individual colours and a corner radius applied over the named theme (or over the player's own when no theme is named). This is how a chapter sets "raised #24242E and radius 4" without shipping a whole theme file, and the Chapter tab's appearance section writes it.

dependsOn.description: Quest ids or aliases. May refer to quests in other files. A reference that resolves to nothing is an error: the quest could never unlock.

dependencyLines.description: Per-line overrides, keyed by the id of the dependency the line comes from. Only the axes named for a line are overridden; the rest fall back to the chapter's `dependencyStyle`, and then to the built-ins. A key that names a dependency the quest does not have is dead weight, and the editor drops an entry once it sets nothing.

prerequisiteMode.description: Overrides the chapter's setting for this quest.

minRequired.description: How many dependencies must be satisfied, replacing the mode's own count: this is how "any three of these five" is written. The mode still decides the *bar* each one must reach — completed, or merely started — so `one_started` with minRequired 2 means "any two of these, started". May not exceed the number of dependencies.

x.description: Canvas position. The shipped chapters sit on a 32-unit grid; the editor snaps to 8.

shape.description: The node's outline, each drawn at its own true proportions. "none" draws no panel at all: the node is its icon, and the whole square is clickable. Every other outline is hit-tested by its own pixels, so a click lands on exactly what is drawn.

rotation.description: How far the node is turned, in degrees clockwise. Every shape can be turned: a rotation rotates the outline rather than naming a second one, and the node is drawn, clicked and icon-fitted in its turned form. A turned outline is fitted to the node with one uniform scale, so nothing is cut off at the node's edge and nothing is stretched. A full turn is written as 0, because it is the same shape.

iconScale.description: How much of the node the icon fills. The outline caps it: a shape with less room draws the largest item it can hold, so the frames stay comparable. 1.0 is corner to corner; the default leaves a margin so the node's shape reads.

showTitle.description: Draw this quest's name under its node. Off by default: a canvas of fifty names is a wall of text, and the name is on hover for every quest either way.

sequentialTasks.description: Tasks must be done in order: the second cannot be handed in until the first is.

autoClaim.description: Whether this quest's rewards are handed over the moment it completes, overriding the chapter's own `autoClaim` (which in turn defers to the pack setting in index.json). A reward's own `auto` still wins over this. `enabled` pays with a notification, `no_toast` silently, `invisible` with no trace; `disabled` waits for a claim. Rewards that need a decision - a choice reward - are never auto-granted whatever this says.

repeatCooldownTicks.description: Ticks to wait between completions of a repeatable quest. 2400 is two minutes.

exclusiveGroup.description: Quests sharing a group name are mutually exclusive: completing one locks the others for good. Scoped to the chapter.

repeatable.description: Completable more than once. Its timesCompleted survives each completion, and something depending on it stays satisfied.

invisibleUntilTasks.description: With `invisible` also set: shown once this many of the quest's tasks have any progress, as well as when it is completed. The easter-egg case — a quest nobody can see until they have stumbled onto part of it. Without `invisible` it does nothing.

maxCompletableDependents.description: At most this many of the quests that depend on this one may complete; the rest stay locked for good. 0 is no cap. A branch point: the player picks one way, and the other ways close. A dependent already completed stays completed.

hideUntilDependenciesComplete.description: Hidden until this quest's prerequisite *rule* is satisfied — the same rule the card's "2 of 3 met" counts, so minRequired and the started-based modes are honoured. A completed quest is always visible. Leave the field out and the chapter's defaultHideUntilDependenciesComplete decides; write false to opt out of a chapter that hides its quests by default.

hideUntilDependenciesVisible.description: Hidden until at least one of its prerequisites is itself visible. Recursive, so a chain of hidden quests reveals itself one link at a time from its first visible end. A quest with no prerequisites at all is visible, because an empty rule is met - this used to stay hidden, which is the trap the sibling flag's empty case never had. Leave the field out and the chapter's defaultHideUntilDependenciesVisible decides; write false to opt out.

hideDependencyLines.description: Draw no dependency lines arriving at this quest. The quest itself is unaffected, and quests that depend on it still draw their lines to it.

hideTextUntilComplete.description: The reader's card shows no description until the quest is completed — for a quest whose text would give away what it is asking for. The editor always shows it.

hideDetailsUntilStartable.description: The reader's card shows no task or reward details until the quest can be started. REQUIRES stays: a locked quest's prerequisites are what says how to unlock it. The editor always shows everything.

requiresStage.description: A stage the player must have for the quest to be open to them, e.g. my_pack:chapter_one. The one gate here that is per player rather than per team: a quest gated on a stage is open to a player who has it and locked to one who does not, even in the same party. Nothing validates that the stage exists -- one exists by being granted -- so a typo shows up as a quest nobody can open.

anyType.description: A task or a reward. The `type` field chooses the rest of the fields, and each field below names the type it belongs to. A field written for another type is a mistake the validator reports rather than a value anything reads.

type.description: The type's id, e.g. tasked:item. The id decides which of the fields below mean anything.

optional.description: Tasks only. An optional task does not have to be done for the quest to complete, unless every task is optional.

autoSubmitTicks.description: Tasks only. How often the task is re-checked, in ticks, twenty to the second. Left out, the task keeps its type's own cadence — 20 for most, 3 for a stat or a location, 5 for an advancement, 100 for a dimension — which is a sensible interval for how expensive that check is. Set it to override that. There is deliberately no one default here: a single number would be wrong for most of the types it applied to.

conditions.description: Tasks and rewards. Gates that must all hold for a player before the task counts for them, or the reward is paid to them.

item.description: tasked:item (task and reward) — the item to hand over, or to give.

count.description: tasked:item and tasked:item_tag (tasks), tasked:item (reward) — how many.

components.description: tasked:item (task and reward) — 1.21 data components, keyed by component id in the datapack's own spelling. A text component's value is a string holding JSON, as the codec writes it -- the editor writes that form when you pick a renamed item.

consumeItems.description: tasked:item and tasked:item_tag (tasks) — whether handing the task in takes the items. Falls back to the chapter's defaultConsumeItems.

match.description: tasked:item (task) — how closely a carried stack must match: none ignores its data, fuzzy needs the data it names, strict needs the whole stack. Strict is the default, so a file that says nothing keeps the meaning it had before this field existed.

onlyFromCrafting.description: tasked:item (task) — only items the player crafted themselves count.

tag.description: tasked:item_tag (task) — an item tag; any item in it counts.

title.description: tasked:checkmark (task) — the label on the button a player presses.

dimension.description: tasked:dimension and tasked:location (tasks) — the dimension the player has to be in, or the one the location box is in.

biome.description: tasked:biome (task) — the biome to stand in; a #tag counts any biome of it.

structure.description: tasked:structure (task) — the structure to be inside; a #tag counts any of them.

advancement.description: tasked:advancement (task and reward) — the advancement to earn, or to award.

criterion.description: tasked:advancement (task and reward) — one criterion of it instead of the whole advancement; empty for the whole one.

stat.description: tasked:stat (task) — which vanilla statistic to watch.

value.description: tasked:stat, tasked:xp, tasked:kill and tasked:custom (tasks) — the number that counts as enough: the statistic's value, experience handed over, kills, or the handler's count.

ignoreDimension.description: tasked:location (task) — count the box anywhere, instead of only in the dimension above.

position.description: tasked:location (task) — one corner of the box, in blocks, as [x, y, z].

size.description: tasked:location (task) — how far the box reaches from that corner, as [x, y, z].

points.description: tasked:xp (task) — whether the count is experience points (true, the default) or whole levels (false).

fluid.description: tasked:fluid (task) — the fluid to hand over, carried in buckets.

amount.description: tasked:fluid (task) — how much of it, in millibuckets; a bucket is a thousand. tasked:xp (reward) — points, or levels, to give.

observeType.description: tasked:observation (task) — what counts as looking: a block, a tag of them, one block state, a block entity, or an entity. The target below follows this.

toObserve.description: tasked:observation (task) — the block or entity to look at.

timer.description: tasked:observation (task) — how long to look at it, in ticks, twenty to the second.

entityTypeTag.description: tasked:kill (task) — or an entity tag, to count any mob in it. Its own field rather than a # in `entity`, so a tag where an id is expected is an error here as it is everywhere else.

customName.description: tasked:kill (task) — only counts a mob with this name.

nbtFilter.description: tasked:kill (task) — an SNBT filter, for the mobs an id cannot pick out.

id.description: tasked:custom (task and reward) — the id a mod or a script registered a handler for. The validator warns when this build has nothing registered for it.

team.description: Rewards only. Whether this is a one-claim-for-the-team reward. Absent falls back to the tree's defaultTeamReward.

auto.description: Rewards only. When it is handed over: default follows the tree's own setting, enabled gives it on completion, disabled waits for a claim, no_toast gives it without a toast, and invisible grants the same way - the two silent names are FTB Quests' vocabulary rather than a behaviour.

excludeFromClaimAll.description: Rewards only. Claim all leaves this one for its own press.

ignoreRewardBlocking.description: Rewards only. Give it even while the team's rewards are being held.

randomBonus.description: tasked:item (reward) — up to this many more, rolled at random on top of the count.

onlyOne.description: tasked:item (reward) — skip it if the player already carries this item.

levels.description: tasked:xp (reward) — give whole levels rather than points, which is the default. The task's own switch is `points`, and it reads the other way: true there counts points.

table.description: tasked:random, tasked:loot, tasked:all_table and tasked:choice (rewards) — the reward table to roll, by id: a file under reward_tables/, named without its .json suffix. The roll happens when the reward is collected.

inline.description: tasked:random, tasked:loot, tasked:all_table and tasked:choice (rewards) — the table itself, for a reward that is its own roll.

permissionLevel.description: tasked:command (reward) — the permission level the command runs at; 2 is a command block's.

command.description: tasked:command (reward) — run as the player when the reward is collected, without the leading slash.

silent.description: tasked:command (reward) — do not say in chat that it ran.

stage.description: tasked:stage (task and reward) — the stage the player has to have, or the one to set. Any id: a stage exists by being granted, so there is no list to pick from and nothing to validate.

remove.description: tasked:stage (reward) — take the stage away instead of granting it.
